newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-NORMAN TWO SHOTS OFF THE PACE AFTER OPENING 69.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-NORMAN TWO SHOTS OFF THE PACE AFTER OPENING 69.

text.p: World number one Greg Norman fired a three under par 69 on Thursday to trail the first round leaders by two shots in his final tournament before taking a three-month break because of a back problem.

The 41-year-old Australian, who is hosting his own event, finished in a group of players, including defending champion Craig Parry, chasing compatriot Lucas Parsons and Dutchman Rolf Muntz in the Greg Norman Classic at Royal Melbourne.
Although Norman was pleased with his form, he expressed disappointment over a strike by television workers that blacked out live coverage in his native Australia.
"Maybe there'll be record crowds because they can't watch it on television," said Norman, who won his fifth Australian Open title on Sunday.
Earlier this week Norman said he would take a lengthy rest during which he planned to undergo tests on a lingering back complaint.
Norman said he was satisfied with his round after making amends for one or two "mental mistakes" with his putter.
Parsons, who struggled badly on the U.S. PGA Tour this year, birdied the first four holes in a blistering start to share the lead with Muntz.
